label: Aristotle, Physics VIII.4, 254b27-33…: Whatever is moved in a respect by nature and by itself is…
interpretation: Of natural motions, those of things moved by themselves are moved by something (255b32-33). For animals, 'it is not unclear whether it is moved by something, but how one must distinguish in it the mover and the moved' (254b27-33): the mover is the moving part. The reading asserts only that the motion has a per se mover in that respect; it leaves open which being the mover is, and does not assert that the mover is another than the whole.
